id: title:Gilbert09:stop retrying a mysql server out of memory error

review.posthog_relevance: Warehouse ingestion reliability: prevents unnecessary retries of MySQL connections failing with error 1041 (database memory exhaustion), reducing wasted resources and helping diagnose host resource limits.
review.reason: Adds MySQL error 1041 to the set of non-retryable errors, treating it as a static server-side resource exhaustion rather than a transient failure. This prevents warehouse ingestion jobs from retrying connections that will not succeed, reducing wasted retry attempts and aiding diagnosis of database host resource exhaustion. Tests are included.
review.uncertainty: Assessment relies on supplied hunk and behavior description; no independent verification of actual production impact or complete context of the warehouse ingestion workflow.

observations.limitations: Only supplied hunk IDs are cited. No score assigned.

observations.behavior: Adds MySQL error 1041 (ER_OUT_OF_RESOURCES) to the set of non-retryable errors, treating it as a static server-side resource exhaustion rather than a transient failure.
observations.code_quote: "(1041,": "Your MySQL/MariaDB server ran out of memory (error 1041). This usually means mysqld or another process on the host is using all available memory, or the host needs more swap space. Free up memory on your database server, raise mysqld's memory limit (for example via 'ulimit'), or add swap space, then resync.",
observations.posthog_connection: This change prevents PostHog warehouse ingestion jobs from retrying MySQL connections that fail with error 1041, recognizing that the database host has exhausted available memory and retries would not succeed. This could reduce wasted retry attempts and help users diagnose resource exhaustion on their database hosts.

observations.behavior: Adds a test case asserting that MySQL error 1041 is classified as a non-retryable error, covering both raw pymysql string representation and the wrapped string format used by Temporal.
